Box: A Box Collision Shape
Circle: A Circular Collision Shape
Simple Polygon: A 'best fit' convex polygon with up to 8 sides will be created to represent the shape.
Complex Polygon: Accurate collision for concave polygons - automatically triangulated for precise collision detection.
Chain: A **still** one sided collision object that represents a chain of points. This is suitable for open paths.
Chain (reversed): As above but collisions happen on the other side of the shape.
Soft Body: Deformable physics body made from spring-connected particles. Supports complex polygons with holes.
Comma-separated group names this body belongs to (e.g., 'terrain,solid'). Leave empty to belong to all groups. Use 'none' to belong to no groups.
Comma-separated group names this body collides with (e.g., 'terrain,solid'). Leave empty to collide with all groups. Use 'none' to collide with nothing.

Damping ratio. Controls how quickly oscillations settle.
Internal pressure for volume preservation. Higher values push particles outward to maintain the body's shape.
Strength of shape preservation. Gently pulls particles toward their original relative positions to help restore the body's shape after deformation.
Size of the particles that are used to simulate the soft body. Smaller values give finer detail but more particles - smaller values are much harder to control.

Maximum allowed stretch of spring connections as a multiple of rest length. Lower values maintain shape better under impact but may be less flexible. 2.0 = springs can stretch to double their rest length.
